title: Local users can take over loopback Proxiware CDP
description: Before remediation, Chrome exposed an unauthenticated TCP CDP listener on 127.0.0.1:9222. The Playwright adapter connected to that listener, so a local unprivileged process could request the CDP WebSocket, read provider cookies, and evaluate JavaScript in the authenticated browser context. A dynamic proof succeeded as nobody. The current worktree adds an owner-based nftables ACL and dedicated systemd identity; production verification remains required.
root_cause: The Chrome service and CdpProxiwareBrowser in deploy/earn-proxy-proxiware-chrome.service and app/services/proxiware_browser.py did not add OS-level authentication to the loopback CDP TCP listener, allowing any local user to attach.
intended_behavior: Only the isolated browser observer and explicitly guarded swap worker may access the Proxiware browser session; unrelated local users must be denied.

trace.description: Starts Chromium with a TCP remote-debugging listener bound to 127.0.0.1.
Connects Playwright to the loopback CDP endpoint without an OS-user authentication layer.
Exposes page JavaScript evaluation through the attached authenticated browser context.

conditions.description: The attacker only needs local code execution as an unrelated unprivileged account.
The pre-fix Chrome unit is enabled and the browser has an authenticated provider session.

execution.attacker_perspective: An unrelated local Unix user on the VPS.
payloads: Open the returned DevTools WebSocket and issue Network.getAllCookies or Runtime.evaluate(document.cookie)
instructions: Run the requests as nobody while the pre-fix Chrome service is active.
Attach to an existing provider page through the returned WebSocket.
Read cookies or execute JavaScript in the authenticated page.
execution.expected_result: The pre-fix local user obtains CDP access and session data; the remediated owner ACL rejects the connection unless the process UID is earnproxy-browser.

remediation.strategy: Keep CDP loopback-only and add a kernel-enforced owner ACL, dedicated browser identities, and systemd lifecycle coupling.

code_changes.fixed_code: Install a nftables output rule accepting TCP 9222 only for the earnproxy-browser UID and rejecting other UIDs.
Install the ACL before Chrome and remove it when Chrome stops.
Run the guarded swap worker as earnproxy-browser.

likelihood.reason: Any local account or compromised local service could connect without credentials; remote network users cannot reach the loopback bind directly.

impact.reason: CDP grants authenticated provider cookies and arbitrary page JavaScript, enabling provider session takeover.

confidence.reason: The listener and Playwright path are explicit in source and the attack was dynamically reproduced as nobody.

title: Root release follows a raceable database path
description: Release 3082daf used root chown and chmod on the database path and SQLite sidecars after the path came from configuration. The database directory is writable by the earnproxy service account. A compromised process could leave the final path as a symlink before deployment, redirecting root metadata changes to a selected target; the later SQLite backup also reopened the path by name. The current worktree fixes both permission changes and backup reads with no-follow descriptors, pins the backup source FD, and restricts production to the direct database path; deployment verification remains required.
root_cause: The release permission step in deploy/release.sh used path-based chown and chmod instead of no-follow descriptor operations, allowing a compromised earnproxy process to race a replaceable database pathname.
intended_behavior: Root deployment must change permissions only on the configured regular SQLite files and must fail closed on symlinks or non-regular paths.

trace.description: Invokes the descriptor-safe runtime permission helper for the configured database path.
Opens the runtime path with O_NOFOLLOW and a close-on-exec descriptor.
Applies fchown and fchmod only to the validated regular-file descriptor.

conditions.description: The attacker must first compromise or execute code as the earnproxy service account.
The path replacement must occur while a root release is running and before the root metadata operation completes.

execution.attacker_perspective: A compromised earnproxy process with write access to /var/lib/earn-proxy.
payloads: Replace /var/lib/earn-proxy/earn-proxy.db with a symlink to a root-readable target during release.sh
instructions: Wait for a root release to enter the database permission step.
Swap the configured database pathname for a symlink immediately before root chown/chmod in the pre-fix release.
Observe the target ownership or mode change.
execution.expected_result: The pre-fix path-based operation follows the replacement; the remediated helper rejects the symlink with O_NOFOLLOW and changes no target metadata.

remediation.strategy: Use no-follow descriptor operations from the immutable archived release and require regular files.

code_changes.fixed_code: Open with O_NOFOLLOW, fstat for a regular file, then fchown/fchmod the descriptor.

Invoke the helper from $release_dir/deploy after extracting the selected Git revision; pin the SQLite backup source through /proc/self/fd; remove direct path-based chown/chmod and reject custom nested database paths.

likelihood.reason: A compromised earnproxy process can replace the final pathname in its writable runtime directory before a known release; a precise timing race is not required.

impact.reason: Root metadata changes could expose or alter permissions on a root-owned target and undermine deployment isolation.

confidence.reason: The pre-fix root operations and writable runtime directory are explicit; the no-follow regression test reproduces the dangerous symlink case and verifies the target remains unchanged.
